Carter County, TN Tax Sales: How to Buy Properties at Auction

If you’re looking for investment opportunities in Tennessee, Carter County’s tax deed sales are a great place to start. The county auctions off properties with unpaid taxes, giving buyers a chance to pick up real estate—often at a steep discount. But before you jump in, it’s important to understand how these sales work.

Quick Look: Carter County Tax Sale Details

How Carter County Tax Sales Work

Carter County holds online tax deed auctions using GovEase. These sales usually take place in early March, but you should always check the Carter County Chancery Court page for updates.

Steps to Participate

  1. Register on GovEase
    Upload a valid ID, fill out a W-9, and provide proof of funds.
  2. Research the Properties
    Use the Carter County Property Search to review ownership and GIS info.
    If you’re local, drive by the property to see its condition and location.
  3. Understand the Rules
    Sales are final. No refunds. No guarantees.
    A one-year redemption period applies after the auction.
  4. Bid Online
    Bidding starts at the total taxes and fees owed.
    The highest bidder wins, pending court approval.
  5. Pay Immediately
    Payment is due on auction day by certified check, money order, or cash.
  6. Wait for Court Approval
    The Carter County Chancery Court reviews and approves all sales, which can take 30 to 45 days.
  7. Watch the Redemption Period
    If the original owner redeems the property within one year, you get your funds back, but not the property.
    If they don’t, you’ll receive a tax deed and gain ownership rights.

Important Things to Know

  • You’re buying “as-is.” There are no warranties on property condition or title.
  • There may be liens. Do a title search to check for unpaid debts or claims.
  • Title insurance may be tricky. You may need to file a quiet title action first.
  • You may have to evict. If someone lives there, legal eviction may be required.
  • All sales are final. Once you bid and win, there are no refunds.

Interesting Facts About Carter County Real Estate

  • Mountain and Lake Access
    Watauga Lake and Roan Mountain add long-term value to nearby properties, especially for vacation or retirement buyers.
  • Lower Cost of Entry
    Property prices are more affordable compared to neighboring urban areas, making it attractive for first-time investors.
  • Tourism Drives Demand
    Short-term rentals, cabins, and mountain getaways are popular due to nearby trails and parks.
  • Small-Town Living, Big-City Access
    Elizabethton offers a quiet setting with nearby amenities in Johnson City.
  • Tax Deed Auctions Offer Real Opportunity
    These annual sales give you a chance to invest in Tennessee real estate for a fraction of market value.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I register on auction day?
No. You must register ahead of time on GovEase and complete the required paperwork.

Do I get the property right after I win?
No. The court must approve the sale, and then there’s a 1-year redemption period.

What if the owner pays off their taxes?
If redeemed, you get your money back but not the property.

Can out-of-state or foreign investors bid?
Yes. Anyone who completes registration through GovEase can participate.

Are there extra costs beyond the winning bid?
Yes. Be prepared for legal fees, title clearing, and possibly eviction costs.

Pro Tips for New Investors

  • Always research title history before bidding.
  • Stick to your budget. Don’t get caught up in bidding wars.
  • Track redemptions so you know when you’ll gain ownership.
  • Expect some risk. This isn’t a guaranteed way to profit.

Why Carter County is Worth a Look

Carter County offers beautiful scenery, low entry prices, and a transparent tax deed process. Investors can find land, cabins, and even homes at below-market prices with the chance for strong returns. Just make sure to research and plan before you bid.
